thesis: LeCun argues that LLMs are a dead-end for general intelligence and that JEPA — a non-generative, joint-embedding world-model architecture — is the right substrate for agents that can predict the consequences of their actions.

chapters.title: HRT is an awesome place to work
Do our models need to be generative?

insights.headline: JEPA predicts embeddings, not pixels or tokens
insights.body: Instead of predicting outputs Y directly from inputs X, JEPA passes both X and Y through encoders and trains a third 'predictor' model to map the embedding of X to the embedding of Y. This sidesteps generation entirely.

insights.headline: Intelligence as a cake: SSL is the bulk
insights.body: LeCun's 2015 meme slide: self-supervised learning is the cake, supervised learning is the icing, reinforcement learning is the cherry. He used it to argue RL alone could never reach human or animal intelligence — too inefficient.

insights.headline: OpenAI was an RL shop before Radford pivoted
insights.body: OpenAI initially focused on RL (Gym, Universe, video games). Alec Radford modified a Google translation Transformer into a next-token predictor trained on 7,000 internal books — that became GPT-1, the unlock that freed models from labeled data.

insights.headline: Video frame prediction blurs because of averaging
insights.body: If a ball can bounce many directions, a pixel-level model forced to output one frame predicts the average of outcomes — which looks like blurry mush. LLMs avoid this because they have independent probability outputs per token.

insights.headline: Possible next frames dwarf atoms in the universe
insights.body: A full-HD frame has ~10^15,000,000 possible pixel configurations vs GPT-2's 50,257-token vocabulary. Enumerating outputs the way LLMs do is mathematically hopeless for video.

insights.headline: Representation collapse: the trivial all-ones solution
insights.body: Joint-embedding networks trained only to maximize similarity discover they can output the same vector for every input. Similarity is perfect, nothing useful is learned. This is the central problem JEPA architectures must solve.

insights.headline: Barlow Twins: force cross-correlation to identity
insights.body: Stéphane Deny and LeCun (2020) built a loss that pushes the cross-correlation matrix between two encoders' neuron outputs toward the identity — diagonal correlations high (matched pairs agree), off-diagonals near zero (neurons stay non-redundant). Derived from Horace Barlow's 1961 neuroscience hypothesis.

insights.headline: DINOv3 hit 88.4% on ImageNet with no labels
insights.body: Released August 2025, DINOv3 reached 88.4% ImageNet accuracy — comparable to the best supervised models (88.6% for the 2020 Google ViT). Authors call it the first time self-supervised matched weakly/supervised on classification.

insights.headline: Don't waste compute predicting unpredictable leaves
insights.body: LeCun's dashcam example: a pixel-generative video model burns most of its capacity predicting random leaf motion. Embeddings let the predictor focus only on salient, predictable features of the scene.

insights.headline: Action-conditioned JEPA = learned world model for robots
insights.body: VJEPA-2 conditions the embedding-space predictor on robot arm control signals. Given a goal-state embedding, a classical optimal-control search over imagined action sequences finds actions whose predicted future embedding matches the goal.

insights.headline: A teen learns to drive in 20 hours; Tesla can't
insights.body: LeCun's challenge: millions of hours of supervised driving data only get you to L2, but a 17-year-old reaches competence in a few hours. The missing ingredient, he claims, is a world model that predicts consequences of actions.

insights.headline: JEPA will eventually replace LLMs
insights.body: Asked whether world-model approaches will replace LLMs, LeCun says: initially they solve different problems, eventually they'll replace LLMs — because LLMs are only good where language itself is the substrate of reasoning.

insights.headline: Use linear probes to audit frozen representations
insights.body: Barlow Twins was evaluated by freezing the encoder and training a single linear layer on ImageNet — that frozen+probe setup hit 73.2%, beating AlexNet's 59.3% supervised baseline. It's the standard recipe for testing whether SSL learned useful features.

insights.headline: Siamese nets started as 1990s signature fraud detection
insights.body: LeCun's joint-embedding lineage traces to Bell Labs in the early 1990s: two copies of a network produced embeddings for pairs of signatures, trained with contrastive positive/negative pairs to detect forgery. Same architecture, 30+ years later, is the path to world models.

quotes.text: Initially, they'll solve different problems. Eventually, they'll replace LLMs.
quotes.speaker: Yann LeCun

quotes.text: If intelligence is a cake, the bulk of the cake is self-supervised learning, the icing on the cake, supervised learning, and the cherry on the cake, reinforcement learning.
quotes.speaker: Yann LeCun

quotes.text: I do not understand how you can even think of building an agentic system without an agentic system having the ability of predicting the consequences of its actions.
quotes.speaker: Yann LeCun

quotes.text: They just take the action and then après moi le déluge, as some famous French kings said.
quotes.speaker: Yann LeCun

quotes.text: It will spend most of its resources predicting the random motion of the leaves on the trees that are bordering the road.
quotes.speaker: Yann LeCun

quotes.text: What is even less classical is you learn a representation of the input that computes a state, an abstract state representation. And you learn the model in that state. And that's JEPA.
quotes.speaker: Yann LeCun

action_items: If you're building agentic systems, ask whether your model can predict the consequence of an action before taking it — if not, you don't have a world model, you have an autocomplete.
When benchmarking self-supervised representations, freeze the encoder and use a linear probe — that's how Barlow Twins/DINO showed their features actually generalize.
Stop trying to predict at the pixel level for video tasks; predict in embedding space so the model can ignore unpredictable noise like wind in leaves.
Read LeCun's 'A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence' (2022) to see the full architecture argument, not just JEPA in isolation.
